     def flush(self):
         tmp, self.cache = self.cache, []
         text = ''.join(tmp)
-        if text.isspace():
-            # Readers drop whitespace tokens other than a bare newline.
+        if not text or text.isspace():
+            # Readers drop whitespace tokens other than a bare newline. An
+            # element right after a child element has no text before it:
+            # an empty token would reach the extensions, which read token[0].
             return ['\n'] * text.count('\n')
         return [text]

metadata.body:
## Summary When a JSX element follows another child element with no text between them, the element body flushed an empty text token. The duplicate extension reads `token[0]` of every token, so `-Eduplicate` stopped on such files with `IndexError: string index out of range`. An empty flush now gives no token, as the `{` child-expression branch already did. ```diff XMLTagWithAttrTokenizer.flush - text == "" -> [""] (empty token) + text == "" -> [] (no token) text is spaces -> one "\n" per newline ``` Changes are in `lizard_languages/tsx.py`, with a tokenizer test in `test/test_languages/testTSX.py`. ## Evidence ```tsx function Panel() { return

x

; } ``` - **Before** (master `f9323a80`), `lizard -Eduplicate panel.tsx`: ``` IndexError: string index out of range ``` **After:** ``` 3 1 10 0 3 Panel@1-3@panel.tsx ``` - Tokenizer: `
x
` gave `['
', '
x
', '', '', '
']`; it now gives no `''`. - The empty tokens were also counted as tokens: in `test_slash_in_text_does_not_open_a_regex` the token count of `Rates`, which has sibling `` elements, goes from 47 to 45. The expectation is updated. - In a real React front end, 6 of 752 `.tsx` files stopped `-Eduplicate` this way; with the fix all of them are read. - Test suite (excluding `test_website*.py`, which needs Flask): 3078 passed, with the same 29 failures as master. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way **Blast Radius:** JSX/TSX tokens Token counts drop for components with adjacent child elements. CCN, NLOC and function bounds are unchanged.
